newsitem.title: USA: Clinton holds narrow lead in Florida - poll.
newsitem.headline: Clinton holds narrow lead in Florida - poll.

text.p: President Bill Clinton holds a four-point lead over Republican challenger Bob Dole in the race for Florida's 25 electoral votes, according to poll results published in the Tampa Tribune on Friday.

The Tampa Tribune/Newschannel 8 poll of 828 likely voters, conducted on Monday and Tuesday, had 46 percent of voters planning to vote for Clinton, while 42 percent favored Dole. Reform Party candidate Ross Perot had the support of five percent of voters.
Seven percent of the electorate was undecided and the survey's margin of error was 3.5 percent.
The newspaper said a comparable poll last month had Clinton leading by three points, with 47 percent of voters to Dole's 44 percent.
Pollster Robert Joffee of Mason-Dixon Political/Media Research told the newspaper that the result likely would come down to whose voters turned out most heavily on Tuesday.
He noted that about two-thirds of the undecided voters said they were Democrats.
Florida has not gone Democratic in a presidential election since 1976. It is considered a must-win state for Dole.
